prompt: Design state and caching for a multi-region product catalog with flexible attributes, search/browse views, high read traffic, inventory references, bursty viral products, regional outages, privacy deletion, and a small operations team. Choose relational, document, key/value, wide-column, cache and search responsibilities from evidence rather than using every store.
directAnswer: Begin with operation and invariant inventory. Product authoring needs stable identity, schema/version validation, uniqueness and controlled multi-field change; inventory reservation remains an authoritative conditional transition and must not be implemented as an evictable cache value. Flexible product display aggregates that are usually read together can fit a document model when document growth, update contention and duplication are bounded. Key/value access fits exact-ID projections or session state. Wide-column fits high-volume partition-key-plus-range access such as time-ordered history when partition size and repair are controlled. Search is a derived index, not product truth. Define the source of truth for every field and a reconciliation direction. Model access patterns before schema: key, predicates, sort, page size, result size, read/write/burst rate, consistency, atomic scope, retention and deletion. Choose partition/shard keys using cardinality and hottest-key distributions, including secondary indexes; viral products need read replication/cache/coalescing and perhaps controlled write allocation, not blind salting of an invariant. State read/write concerns or consistency per operation, including read-your-writes and projection freshness. Use versioned immutable cache keys where possible; for mutable entries use cache-aside or a deliberately justified write-through path with versioned fill/invalidation, bounded TTL plus jitter, negative-cache bounds, request coalescing, stale policy and origin admission. Never use cache presence as authorization truth or let a security lookup fail open. Write-behind needs a durable ordered buffer, idempotent sink and reconciliation; otherwise cache loss loses acknowledged writes. Size memory from serialized value plus metadata/allocator/replication/client overhead and headroom, not item payload alone. Test cold start, full eviction, hot key, skew, origin slowdown, failover, partial invalidation, replica lag, rebalance and repair. Observe user correctness/latency/freshness, per-operation store latency, throttle/reject, partition skew, hottest keys, item sizes, hit/miss by outcome, eviction/expiry/invalidation, fill latency, origin amplification, replication/repair and deletion backlog. Recovery identifies authority, prevents stale refill, restores origin before warming gradually, reconciles derived stores and proves privacy deletion across caches, indexes, backups according to policy. Compare the simplest relational-plus-cache-plus-search design against document or wide-column alternatives; select only stores whose operational benefit exceeds new failure, security, cost and skill burden.
foundation: A data store is selected from access patterns, atomic and consistency scope, failure behavior and team capacity. A cache is a controlled copy with explicit authority, freshness, invalidation and origin-failure behavior.
reasoningSteps: Inventory operations invariants and state owners.
Measure access patterns distributions and growth.
Choose data model and atomic scope per workload.
Design partition keys indexes and hot-key handling.
Name consistency and session guarantees per operation.
Design cache keys fill write invalidation TTL stale and failure modes.
Calculate memory throughput origin and failure capacity.
Design privacy security repair backup restore and reconciliation.
Compare alternatives and prove with representative fault/load evidence.
seniorAnswer: I would start with the smallest portfolio that preserves ownership: an authoritative transactional product/inventory boundary, derived display/search projections, and a cache only for replaceable read paths. I would show one viral key, one regional isolation, one stale invalidation and one privacy deletion end-to-end, including what becomes unavailable and how every copy is reconciled.
weakAnswer: Use MongoDB for flexible JSON, Cassandra for scale, Redis for speed, Elasticsearch for search, and eventual consistency everywhere.
whyWeak: It adds four state owners without access patterns, invariants, atomic scope, consistency, partition keys, invalidation, deletion, recovery, cost or team-operability evidence.

evidence.proves: input to partition and capacity design

followUps.prompt: When would you embed versus reference documents?
followUps.answer: Embed data read and changed with the parent when size and update contention remain bounded; reference independently owned, high-cardinality, frequently changing or shared entities. Validate real document growth and query paths.

followUps.prompt: Why can a 99% hit ratio still be bad?
followUps.answer: The 1% misses may be expensive, concentrated on critical or large keys, amplified concurrently, or overload the origin; hit ratio also says nothing about stale or unauthorized hits.

followUps.prompt: How do you warm a cache after an outage?
followUps.answer: Restore and protect origin capacity, admit/coalesce fills, prioritize critical hot keys, limit concurrency, use version-aware population and observe origin/latency/freshness. Bulk warm only from a measured plan.

followUps.prompt: How does privacy deletion affect caches?
followUps.answer: Track copy owners and key versions, invalidate/purge bounded layers, prevent stale refill, delete authoritative and derived state per policy, handle backups by retention/legal design, and audit completion without logging sensitive payloads.
